To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Gaussian Information Bottleneck (GIB) problem is efficiently solvable and has an analytical solution, (2) the optimal GIB solution is bounded from above (and thus, is not optimal) by non-linear Canonical Correlation Analysis and (3) the GIB solution can be used to provide an efficient representation of any arbitrary dataset (in the IB-sense), which is bounded from above, by non-linear CFA.

(1) The optimal Gaussian embedding of the data is bounded from above and below by non-linear CAA and the GIB respectively; and (2) The optimal embedding is achieved by a simple, linear transformation of the data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning a representation of a set variables, which is as informative as possible about a target variable.
a fundamental question in statistics: how to find the best representation of data in the Gaussian sense, and what are the fundamental limits for this task?
the fundamental limit of the Information Bottleneck, which we find to be Gaussian.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our Gaussian lower bound is an important step towards the understanding of the IB curve and the GIB.
the Gaussian distribution is the most efficient (in the IB framework) and simplest (in the statistical framework) data representation.
the IB curve is the optimal trade-off curve between complexity (MI) and prediction (MI), and that the GIB curve is the optimal curve for Gaussian distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gaussian IB provides a fundamental limit for the performance of any IB method, in particular, the GIB.
the GIB is not only an optimal representation, but also a fundamental limit for the ability to Gaussianize data-sets.
, in the Gaussian case, the GIB is the optimal solution for the IB, and it is also the best approximation for the IB in the general case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GIB can serve as a practical and efficient method for solving complex information-theoretic problems in a linear way, with a provable performance guarantee.
Gaussianization is not only a practical tool for data analysis, but also a fundamental property of any arbitrary data set.
the GIB is not only an efficient and practical method for solving the IB, it is in fact a lower bound for the IB in general.
